complexity.correctness_reason: A word of length 1000 — permitted by the stated constraints (word.length <= 1000) — recurses roughly 1000 frames deep and exceeds CPython's default recursion limit, raising RecursionError.
complexity.notes: Recursion is elegant but un-Pythonic here: word[1:] copies the remaining string at every level (O(L^2) time and O(L^2) peak stack-held characters), whereas an iterative loop over characters with node = node.children[c] is O(L). Dict keys are single characters from a fixed alphabet, so hash collisions are bounded and lookups are O(1) worst case.
complexity.summary: Recursive trie where each node holds a dict of children keyed by single characters and a terminal flag; insert/search/startsWith recurse on word[1:], and the per-level string slicing makes each operation quadratic in the word length L rather than linear.
